extracted.intended_audience: Investor Relations Officers (IROs), corporate IR teams, and compliance/legal professionals responsible for IR websites
extracted.subtask_short: IR website SEC compliance best practices
extracted.subtask_description: Practical best-practice checklist for designing and maintaining an Investor Relations website that meets current SEC disclosure, non-GAAP, cybersecurity, and ESG reporting expectations. Focuses on website content organization, update processes, technical controls, and disclosure presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and accurate SEC filings and financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC enforcement emphasizes the importance of timely and accurate filings (e.g., Form 4, Section 13D/13G); failures to file on time can result in significant penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites recent SEC enforcement actions and fines as motivation to ensure timely filings; IR websites should support timely disclosure by enabling prompt publication and clear access to required filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customized investor content
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand investor preferences for reviewing disclosures and tailor the content on the IR website accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design site sections and content formats (summaries, FAQs, detailed filings) to match how investors prefer to consume disclosure information so material items are visible and understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Having access to website tools allows companies to update their IR website with the latest information promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use site administration tools and processes that enable near-instant posting of filings, press releases, and updates to minimize delay between an event and public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automate reporting processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize software that can automate parts of the reporting process to reduce the risk of human error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include using newswires (e.g., Businesswire) or other automation tools to publish filings and announcements consistently and correctly; automation reduces manual slip-ups that can cause filing delays or inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish clear communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Create dedicated sections on the website for legal, financial, and compliance updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segregate and label content for different stakeholder needs (legal notices, investor presentations, compliance updates) so users can find authoritative material and the company can control messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed disclosure history / archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a comprehensive archive section on the IR website for historical SEC filings and financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an accessible filing archive (example: Walmart maintains an archive) so investors can review historical documents; ensure archival materials are complete, searchable, and preserved accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading non-GAAP measures and reconcile with GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC guidance emphasizes avoiding misleading non-GAAP measures and requires clear reconciliation with GAAP financials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-GAAP metrics must be presented coherently with GAAP reconciliations and explanations; the SEC scrutinizes deviations and issues comment letters — ensure transparency, consistency, and justification for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated non-GAAP website section
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a specific section on the website for non-GAAP measures, providing investors easy access to this information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group non-GAAP metrics and related disclosures in one place to improve discoverability and reduce risk of misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed explanations for non-GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer detailed explanations and justifications for using non-GAAP measures, helping investors understand why they are relevant and how they are calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain adjustments, rationale, formulas, and business reasons for each non-GAAP metric; clarity reduces SEC scrutiny and investor confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interactive tools to compare GAAP and non-GAAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate interactive tools such as calculators or comparison charts that allow investors to see the differences between GAAP and non-GAAP measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual and interactive comparisons help investors grasp the impact of adjustments and improve transparency and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly update non-GAAP content
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the non-GAAP information on the website regularly updated to reflect the latest financial data and SEC guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure historical comparatives, reconciliations, and methodology notes are updated each reporting period to preserve consistency and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of non-GAAP information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the website is user-friendly and inclusive for all investors and that non-GAAP information is presented clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content for clarity (plain-language explanations, accessible charts) and follow accessibility best practices so all investors, including those using assistive technologies, can access disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose material cybersecurity incidents promptly (four-business-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: New SEC rules require registrants to disclose any material cybersecurity incidents, specifying nature, scope, timing, and potential or actual material impact, typically within four business days (subject to limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare processes to identify material incidents quickly and publish required 8-K disclosures within regulatory timelines; note exceptions for national security and varied compliance dates/grace periods for smaller companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cybersecurity risk management and governance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must provide annual reports on cybersecurity risk management, strategies, and governance, describing processes for identifying and managing threats and roles of the board and management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear description of cybersecurity governance, risk assessment processes, controls, and oversight responsibilities in annual disclosures to meet SEC expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and maintain an incident response plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and maintain a robust incident response plan to address and mitigate security breaches or cyber threats quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An up-to-date plan enables timely detection, containment, stakeholder communication, and regulatory disclosure to minimize impact and meet reporting deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform regular security audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct frequent and thorough security audits to identify and address vulnerabilities in the website’s infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic testing and audits (pen tests, vulnerability scans, third-party assessments) help find weaknesses before incidents occur and support compliance assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best-in-class data encryption
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize strong encryption protocols for data transmission, especially for sensitive financial information and personal data of investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encrypt data at rest and in transit, use current industry-standard algorithms and properly manage keys to protect investor data and filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce strict access controls and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement access controls and authentication processes to restrict unauthorized access to sensitive website areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply least-privilege access, multi-factor authentication for administrative users, logging, and role-based controls to reduce insider and external risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain up-to-date website technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure all website software is regularly updated to protect against known vulnerabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patch management, dependency updates, and proactive technology refresh reduce exposure to exploits that could compromise disclosures or investor data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align ESG/climate disclosures with evolving regulatory frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: SEC proposed changes and EU ESRS are moving toward more detailed, comparable climate-related and sustainability disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to provide decision-useful, consistent climate and ESG information (risks, metrics, methodologies) so investors can compare and evaluate impacts; monitor rulemaking and align disclosures accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated ESG section on IR website
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a distinct section on the website for ESG-related information, clearly outlining the company’s policies, practices, and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize ESG policies, reports, and metrics to make sustainability information easily discoverable for stakeholders and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interactive data visualization for ESG metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate interactive charts and graphs visually representing the company’s progress and impact in ESG areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualizations help stakeholders understand trends and context for sustainability metrics; interactive tools can allow filtering by year, region, or metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report specific ESG events and regular ESG reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the website with regular ESG reports, including annual sustainability reports and any disclosures related to climate risks and management strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish timely reports on material ESG developments and maintain an archive of past reports to demonstrate trends and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable stakeholder communication on ESG
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a platform for stakeholders to engage in ESG-related discussions, such as forums or Q&A sections, enhancing transparency and stakeholder involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate feedback channels and engagement tools while maintaining moderation and recordkeeping to manage reputational and compliance risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide educational content on ESG standards and frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include informational content explaining ESG standards, such as the ESRS and SEC reporting requirements, to educate stakeholders about the frameworks guiding disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer plain-language guides, methodology notes, and links to standards so users understand the basis and limitations of reported ESG data (example: Lion Electric’s ESG section).
